data.long_meaning: The Romanian name Mircea is derived from the Romanian word 'mir' meaning 'dear' or 'precious'. The name is a common one in Romania and is given to boys. It is also the name of a famous Romanian ruler, Prince Mircea the Elder. The name Mircea carries the meaning “My Dear” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Mircea usually hope their child will grow to embody my dear and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Mircea I the Old (1386-1418), was a prince of Wallachia who is considered the founder of the Old Dynasty. He was a skilled diplomat and military leader, who managed to resist the Mongol invasion, and later successfully defended against the Hungarian invaders. Mircea’s rule is characterized by the consolidation of the power of the Wallachian principality, its expansion, and the establishment of its independence from the Hungarian and Polish rule.

Mircea Cipariu (1593-1641), was a Moldavian boyar and voivode of Moldavia. He is best known for his successful resistance against the Ottoman invasions, particularly the Battle of Hocimă, where he managed to repel the Ottoman army despite being outnumbered. Mircea’s rule is characterized by his military prowess and his ability to maintain Moldavia’s independence from the Ottoman Empire for several decades.
